record.paper_title: Quasiwypukłość i otwarte problemy analizy funkcjonalnej
record.original_question: Restrict Morrey's rank-one-convexity versus quasiconvexity problem to real-valued functions on 2 by 2 matrices that depend only on the Euclidean norm of the matrix and on its determinant. In this restricted class, does rank-one convexity imply quasiconvexity?

evidence.quote: Również ten wariant hipotezy Morreya jest pytaniem otwartym.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}$ denote the space of real $2\times 2$ matrices, equipped with the Euclidean (Frobenius) norm $\|X\| = \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(X^T X)}$, and let $\det X$ denote the determinant of $X$.

A function $f:\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called rank-one convex if for every $X,Y\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}$ with $\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le 1$ the function $t\mapsto f(X+tY)$ is convex on $\mathbb{R}$.

A locally bounded Borel function $f:\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}\to\mathbb{R}$ is called quasiconvex (in the sense of Morrey) if for every $X\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}$, every bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with $|\partial\Omega|=0$, and every smooth compactly supported $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^2)$,
$$\int_\Omega f(X+\nabla\varphi(x))\,dx \;\ge\; f(X)\,|\Omega|.$$

Consider the restricted class $\mathcal{F}$ consisting of all functions $f:\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2}\to\mathbb{R}$ of the form
$$f(X) = g(\|X\|,\det X)$$
for some function $g:[0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$.

Question: Is it true that every rank-one convex function $f\in\mathcal{F}$ is also quasiconvex?
artifact.status_search_result: Morrey's conjecture in the planar case (2×2 matrices) remains a major open problem in the calculus of variations. Recent work on the volumetric–isochoric split and isotropic energies depending on singular values and determinant (e.g., the "magic" function studied by Voss, Martin, Neff and collaborators, 2022) has reduced certain subcases to specific candidate energies but has not resolved the restricted version where the integrand depends only on the Frobenius norm and determinant. No proof or counterexample is currently known for this restricted class.

status_evidence.title: Morrey's Conjecture for the Planar Volumetric-Isochoric Split
status_evidence.snippet: For planar volumetric-isochorically split energies... the question of whether rank-one convexity implies quasiconvexity can be reduced to whether W_magic^+ is quasiconvex.
status_evidence.claim: The planar Morrey conjecture remains open even in restricted isotropic subclasses depending on singular values and determinant.

status_evidence.title: Numerical approaches for investigating quasiconvexity in the context of Morrey's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Whether or not rank-one convexity implies quasiconvexity in the planar case is considered one of the major open problems in the calculus of variations.
status_evidence.claim: The planar Morrey conjecture is still open.
